From Drug Dependency to Horse Whisperer

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
From Drug Dependency to Horse Whisperer

A young girl, Angelique enters the circular paddock, with a horse on a long rein. Standing in the middle she does what is called lunging the horse, leading the horse around the ring. The horse keeps to the extreme edge of the paddock, cantering fast, making no contact. Natasha (Tash) Lacey enters and takes over, the horse slows down circles closer gradually closing the circle with a bowed head, he is wanting to connect to join-Up with Natasha. The difference in the way the horse behaves relates to the amount of openness and anger the person has. Angelique is overcoming addiction problems. Natasha, her counsellor, is treating her in this horse based therapy.

29 year old, Natasha Lacey is an Equine Assisted Psychotherapist. Her patients are people who are dealing with addiction be it food, alcohol or drugs. Equine therapy aka equine- assisted therapy (EAT) is a form of therapy that involves interactions and activities with horses that hone to the patients own state of mind at the time. Increasingly this has become a form of treatment for anxiety, depression and addiction.


Further information:
Research has shown horses are hyper sensitive to body language. As prey animals this is how they have survived for thousands of years. Their reactions to our heart rate, moods and micro-nuances can give us feedback that is extremely accurate to what is locked in our subconscious. Natasha knows it works; this was part of her own healing journey.

Natasha bonded with these powerful beasts at eight years old when mourning the death of her father, her best friend Chelsea, a horse rider got her on to her pony ‘Caramel Crunch’. She never looked back, spending most of her time at the riding school and livery yard, Lane Stables, riding, grooming and tacking the horses, mucking out the stables every day after school.
 
When retired race horse ‘Bar of Gold’ aka Boggie came into Natasha’s life she was 14. He was scrawny and ugly looking, Natasha rehabilitated him and then started competing with Boggie making the Western Province Eventing team in 2007 and then a year late the Western Province Showjumping team. For Natasha who had been diagnosed with anxiety disorder at school rehabilitating horses became not only her passion but her safety net.

But as her showjumping and eventing success grew, so did Natasha’s anxiety she was battling with a alcohol and drug abuse and an eating disorder, In 2016 after a suicide attempt Natasha, 25 years old was admitted into Healing Wings Rehab on the outskirts of Nelspruit in Mpumalanga.

It was while at rehab that Natasha started becoming involved in the horses there. As she had rehabilitated horses in the past, here the horses helped her heal. This led her to studying horse communication, learning the equine language through Join-Up – a process in which the human communicates with the horse through body language and the horse replies with different gestures. Join – Up is the vision and teaching method of renowned horse whisperer Monty Roberts, who I have done a CB story on and we have wonderful visuals of some of his ‘talking’ to horses here in South Africa.

Natasha, stayed on at Healing Wings, becoming a volunteer and studied Equine Assisted Psychotherapy. EAP is an alternative to traditional talk therapy. It makes use of the predictable behaviours of horses by having the patient, counsellor and equine therapist in a space with the horse. The patient is then asked to interact with the horse through a series of games or challenges. The way in which the individual attempts to interact with the horse and responds to the horses and how the horse reacts to the patient’s behaviour, can shed light on his and her issues and mental state.

In 2018, Natasha trained under US equine therapist Jess Shokey,- who has been a frequent visitor to the centre. Last year Natasha started the equine programme. Horse or equine therapy has huge potential as a therapeutic tool which the centre sees in their residents/ patients.

Cutting edge research, shows that horses are responsive to our heart's electromagnetic field. This and the fact that horses have the largest limbic system, beside humans, of any land mammal make them emotionally capable of connection to humans in some very amazing ways. For Natasha there is nothing so magical or empowering as that bond and what it does she says to the inner rehab.

Natasha is now four years sober she’s now training other staff members in this form of therapy for their patients She’s become very much part of the rehab family, this year marrying counsellor and co-ordinator at the centre, David Lacey. Her own journey has made her a remarkable advocate of what we human’s can learn from these noble beasts and how she puts that into practice day by day.

A feel good insert.

Script:


It’s the one animal you can do so much with on and off the confidence they can give you, the self esteem that grows inside with them, shows and allows you to say hey I am actually good at this thing

V/O
Natasha Lacey is an equine therapist.

Equine or horse therapy involves horses interacting with people to help them heal. An experiential form of therapy, the patient does set activities and simple tasks with the horse during a session. The way they approach the activities gives an understanding of the personality or mental state of the patient.…..it’s also simply about being able to bond with the horse.

V/O
Natasha works as a counsellor at Healing Wings, a drug rehabilitation centre on the outskirts of Nelspruit.

Link
The patients here, young and old, have been battling to escape the tentacles of addiction...hard drugs, alcohol and serious eating disorders.

Natasha: Its one of the darkest places you can be… a place no mans land you have either hit rock bottom or you are on your way there,

V/O
Natasha knows this because she has travelled this road of addiction
She was eight years old when her father died and it was in horses she found her salvation,

Natasha: I had a really good friend Chelsea and she introduced me to horses… one day she said don’t you want to get on…I got on this tiny little pony Caramel Crunch….and from then I was hooked That sort of pulled me out of the hole that I was in.

V/O
She went from strength to strength at 17 showjumping and eventing for Western Province, but the pressure of the lifestyle began to get the better of her.

Link
In her twenties, Natasha seemed to be leading the life. A cabin attendant with a leading airline, she travelled the world and partied in every city. But she was hiding some dark secrets

Natasha: You would think there was nothing wrong there but I was living a double life…when we would get to layover destination I would get to bar and drink and party because I was in denial about the truth about who I was and what I am doing.

Link
It was only a matter of time before she would hit rock bottom ...and it happened in dramatic style 

Natasha: I got into my Moms car I went driving onto Rhodes Drive… I was driving to my ex boyfriend’s house I knew and he had the drugs. I had my Vodka Red Bull in the glass in the cup holder with the bottle of vodka in the back. I lost control coming down Camps Bay and rolled my mom’s car down the mountain. …someone’s construction fence stopped me and car was completely trashed, luckily no one else was caught in the accident because I would have killed them.

Mum Penny ON SKYPE
I always thought I could help her myself because when you are a mom you think you can ,heal the world and you can protect your child from everything. It took me a long long time to accept that I couldn’t help her.

FADE TO BLACK
Pic of Dawn…bird sounds

V/O
In 2016, Nataha ended up at here at Healing Wings.

Natasha: I thought I was coming to Holiday Camp and ride horses chill on the dam, I thought it was going to be like the clinic I was in but it was completely different you have got to tell the incidence that have happened in your life your life story you’ve got to be honest, what changed was I started to see there were other me’s here, other people who had screwed up as well I started to see you can recover from this and for once there was hope in my life

V/O
Part of Natasha’s healing journey was reconnecting with horses here at the rehab, where horse riding was an option.

Natasha :Horses they show their emotions they put their boundaries down they tell us what they want the big heart they have they want to follow you, they want a leader and They are counting on that person.

V/O
After a year, Natasha transitioned to being a volunteer and a year later stayed on as a counsellor using her passion and expertise in expanding the stables and bringing in equine therapy for the residents.

Link: Two years ago Natasha trained under American equine therapist Jess Shokey,- who has been a frequent visitor to the centre. It took her own understanding of healing with horses to a new level

Natasha: She really opened my eyes up to the more therapeutic side of it the psychotherapy she made it more on a personal level with the resident why not have a companion with you and if you do something wrong the horse might show you something in his body language or you might get an activity wrong that we can help you with.

Angie: I don’t know how to describe you sense this major sense of compassion. They don’t shy away from your affection They will either come and nudge you with their head,

V/O
When Angelique Kennedy arrived here with an eating disorder, she was skin and bone weighing 33kgs.

Derek: That’s dangerously thing.
With my eating disorder it had a way of taking over
… I had a problem with alcohol and that just fuelled my eating disorder.
Derek: Angie looking at you now, how have you got over this?
It wasn’t easy I don’t think I will ever be over I think my eating disorder will stay with me for whole life but in this setting people push and motivated me and being with the horses s just the silent comfort when you feel like no body understands you

Link:
The renowned American horse trainer Monty Roberts, who uses what he calls join up as the core of his methods, has had a massive influence on Natasha's life and healing. 

V/O
We interviewed Monty when he came to South Africa a few years ago….

Derek: Monty that was totally impromptu we were passing by and you noticed this horse wanted to play.
Monty: Ya and the horse is a little bored out here and a new guy comes by and he’s saying hello, so I said Hello to him. It’s just a natural kind of conversation thing like passing a friend on a street.

V/O
Monty cracked the code of human and horse communication…. He called the process Join Up.

Natasha: It’s a communication with your body language person and the horse, so you have to be talking to your horse through your body and if you do it clearly and correctly the horse will show you certain gestures. It s what I base a lot of my therapeutic practices with the girls and guys here and when you get the moment of Join Up, the horse actually stops just at a 45 degree angle so it’s a level of trust and willingness of openness from the resident that horse see because the horse is looking for a follower.

Natasha: Your eye on his eye and you just gesture for him to go…

V/O
It takes time, and patience as I soon found out.

Derek: Straight in the eye..
Natasha: There you go

V/O
But eventually

Natasha: So it’s all about body language..there you go
Derek: ….. Go Choccy

Megan: Watching Tash grow to the person I met five years ago now and watching these stables grow with her has been really phenomenal in just helping Tash to learn to grow to have this freedom we went from having four horses to now whole stable I want to say she grew with the equine therapy.

Link
Natasha hasn't touched drugs or alcohol for more than four years and her own journey has made her an advocate for what we can learn from these noble beasts 

V/O
And Just before lockdown she married David Lacey programme director and counsellor at Healing Wings

Derek: So David do you come second to the horses?
David: Well on her trailer there’s a sticker that says take my boyfriend leave my horse so on paper I am first but in reality the horses might be first.

Penny
Derek: seeing Tasha these days.
Penny: ITo have a child that is healthy and well clean and sober I think I’ve won jackpot…gorgeous Dave in the picture.as well when I think how close I came to losing her I get quiet shaky…hind sight 20 20 leading up to it I thought it will be okay until its not and you think jeepers if I don’t do something soon I am not going to have a child. …

Derek: How do you change when you are bonding with a horse
Natasha: I think I become a lot more secure in myself because I know what I am doing.
Derek: Does it take you back?
Natasha: It does it’s a youth feeling when I as little. I see that a horse is also stubborn and immature and they like to play as well. I can be serious sometimes but when I want to have fun I can have fun as well.

But as her showjumping and eventing success grew, so did Natasha’s anxiety she was battling with a alcohol and drug abuse and an eating disorder, In 2016 after a suicide attempt Natasha, 25 years old was admitted into Healing Wings Rehab on the outskirts of Nelspruit in Mpumalanga. It was while at rehab that Natasha started becoming involved in the horses there. As she had rehabilitated horses in the past, here the horses helped her heal. This led her to studying horse communication, learning the equine language through Join-Up – a process in which the human communicates with the horse through body language and the horse replies with different gestures. Join – Up is the vision and teaching method of renowned horse whisperer Monty Roberts, who I have done a CB story on and we have wonderful visuals of some of his ‘talking’ to horses here in South Africa. Natasha, stayed on at Healing Wings, becoming a volunteer and studied Equine Assisted Psychotherapy. EAP is an alternative to traditional talk therapy. It makes use of the predictable behaviours of horses by having the patient, counsellor and equine therapist in a space with the horse. The patient is then asked to interact with the horse through a series of games or challenges. The way in which the individual attempts to interact with the horse and responds to the horses and how the horse reacts to the patient’s behaviour, can shed light on his and her issues and mental state. In 2018, Natasha trained under US equine therapist Jess Shokey,- who has been a frequent visitor to the centre. Last year Natasha started the equine programme. Horse or equine therapy has huge potential as a therapeutic tool which the centre sees in their residents/ patients. Cutting edge research, shows that horses are responsive to our heart's electromagnetic field. This and the fact that horses have the largest limbic system, beside humans, of any land mammal make them emotionally capable of connection to humans in some very amazing ways. For Natasha there is nothing so magical or empowering as that bond and what it does she says to the inner rehab. Natasha is now four years sober she’s now training other staff members in this form of therapy for their patients She’s become very much part of the rehab family, this year marrying counsellor and co-ordinator at the centre, David Lacey. Her own journey has made her a remarkable advocate of what we human’s can learn from these noble beasts and how she puts that into practice day by day. A feel good insert.
